[Soybean_rust] Symptoms:
Soybean rust (Phakopsora pachyrhizi) symptoms commonly appear on lower leaves after flowering. Initially, lesions form as small gray spots that transition to tan or reddish-brown. These lesions are scattered and appear in yellow areas, becoming translucent when held up to the sun. Mature lesions may contain numerous small pustules, typically found on lower leaf surfaces. The disease is favored by cool, wet conditions or high humidity, and dense canopies provide ideal conditions for its development. The symptoms can be distinguished from similar diseases like bacterial blight and Septoria brown spot by the specific lesion coloration and structure. Compared to Septoria brown spot, Soybean rust tends to show more pronounced yellowing around the lesions. | Often confused with: Soybean_Cyst_Nematode | Often confused with: Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus | Often confused with: Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus

[Bacterial_Pustule] Symptoms:
Bacterial Pustule (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. glycines) symptoms typically appear mid to late season on the upper leaves of the plant. Initial lesions start as small, pale green specks with elevated centers, developing into larger, irregularly shaped infected areas. Each lesion is surrounded by a greenish-yellow halo. A pustule may form in the center of some lesions, usually visible on the lower leaf surface. Notably, bacterial pustule does not cause leaves to tatter as seen in bacterial blight. The disease thrives in hot, wet weather, and certain soybean varieties may be particularly susceptible, while others are marketed as resistant. In comparison to Bacterial Blight, which causes tattered leaves and has angular, reddish-brown lesions with yellow halos, bacterial pustule is characterized by its distinct pale green specks and the absence of leaf tattering. | Often confused with: Bacterial_Blight
